routes.description: Establish that objective moral value, categorical obligation, responsibility, and moral knowledge require a transcendent personal ground that theism supplies and secular humanism does not.
routes.successCriteria: Show that God explains the existence, authority, and human apprehension of moral facts while secular goal-based norms remain conditional on interests that agents may reject.

motionBridge.description: God must provide a more adequate foundation for ethics than secular humanism by grounding objective value, categorical duties, and reliable moral cognition.

centralBridges.description: Objective moral properties and obligations must require a nonphysical ground capable of conferring value and authority.
Theism must connect human moral faculties to moral truth rather than merely explain their causal origin.
The secular account must fail to bind agents who reject human well-being or benefit from exceptions to cooperative norms.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Creation in God's image must supply a basis for human worth, rights, and restraints on harming others.
Theistic belief may support the route by supplying conduct-guiding recognition of objective human worth and obligation.

routes.description: Establish that secular humanism supplies a usable, evidence-responsive ethical framework based on human interests, consequences, cooperation, and correction without requiring divine moral facts.
routes.successCriteria: Show that shared conditions of social life support objective means-end judgments and revisable public norms, while a generic or disputed God adds no demonstrated ethical content or dependable access.

motionBridge.description: Secular humanism must provide a more usable and supportable foundation for ethics than an unspecified and undemonstrated divine ground.

centralBridges.description: Human needs, interests, and interdependence must provide a sufficient starting point for ethical concern and cooperation.
Observable consequences must permit non-subjective judgments about which actions better advance human well-being.
Evidence, reason, empathy, and revision must provide methods for identifying error and improving social norms.
The God proposal must lack demonstrated normative content, stable interpretation, or an inference from divine existence to particular duties.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Unchosen participation in social life must explain why individual indifference does not prevent collective ethical judgment and intervention.
Relationships, empathy, and mutual dependence must support human value without requiring cosmic or intrinsic value.

sections.title: Moral reality and the content of a foundation
sections.rationale: The comparison centrally depends on whether objective moral phenomena require a divine ground and whether invoking God supplies ethical content rather than merely naming an entity.

sections.title: Categorical obligation and goal-based normativity
sections.rationale: A principal burden clash concerns whether ethical requirements must bind independently of chosen ends or can arise from shared interests, social participation, and factual consequences.

sections.title: Moral knowledge, error, and correction
sections.rationale: The rival foundations must explain how moral beliefs connect to truth or justified practice and how mistaken judgments can be detected and corrected over time.

sections.title: Human value and moral motivation
sections.rationale: The comparative routes also depend on whether theism uniquely supports human worth and restraint or whether human relationships and public methods supply adequate reasons for ethical conduct.

sections.title: Divine grounding, specificity, and circularity
sections.rationale: The theistic route must distinguish metaphysical grounding from a religious ethical code while addressing whether identifying God with goodness demonstrates or merely assumes the proposed standard.
